content.title: Kate Hudson and Goldie Hawn Shimmer and Shine in Coordinating Metallic Gowns for Mother-Daughter Date at 2026 Oscars
content.text: 0 seconds of 0 secondsVolume 0%Loading ad00:2500:0000:34 NEED TO KNOW Kate Hudson and her mom, Goldie Hawn, stepped out for the 2026 Oscars in matching metallic gowns on Sunday, March 15The Song Sung Blue star wore a sparkling aquamarine number while her mom wore a shimmery silver and black dressThe duo is celebrating Hudson's Best Actress nomination for her role in Song Sung Blue Kate Hudson and Goldie Hawn are shutting down the 2026 Oscars red carpet! The mother-daughter duo attended the awards ceremony in coordinating sparkling ensembles, matching in metallic gowns upon their arrival at the Dolby Theater in Los Angeles on Sunday, March 15. Goldie Hawn and Kate Hudson at the 2026 Oscars. David Fisher/Shutterstock Hudson dazzled in a strapless teal Armani Privé gown that gave enchanting mermaid-like vibes with its sculpted silhouette encrusted with glittering gems that shimmered like ocean water, adding a luminous, mystical touch to her red carpet look. Goldie Hawn and Kate Hudson at the 2026 Oscars. David Fisher/Shutterstock The Song Sung Blue actress' blonde hair gave Old Hollywood glam, parted to the side and swept entirely onto her right shoulder with big, classic curls. Statement silver jewels by Garatti draped gracefully across her décolletage, complementing her strapless sweetheart neckline. Hawn, whose golden blonde locks were nearly identical to her daughter's 'do, wore an all-black gown with dramatic gloves that matched. The dress featured a low-cut halter top with sheer fabric, stitched with sparkling, silver details that cascaded down into its bodice. Hudson is nominated in the Best Actress category at the 2026 Oscars alongside Jessie Buckley (Hamnet), Rose Byrne (If I Had Legs I’d Kick You), Renate Reinsve (Sentimental Value) and Emma Stone (Bugonia). The nomination is Hudson's second in her acting career; she was previously nominated for Best Supporting Actress for her performance in the 2000 movie Almost Famous at the 2001 Oscars. (Marcia Gay Harden took home that year's trophy for Pollock.) Goldie Hawn and Kate Hudson arrive at the 2026 Oscars. Mike Coppola/Getty Hawn won a Best Supporting Actress Oscar in 1970 for her performance in the movie Cactus Flower, though she did not attend that year's ceremony because she was filming another movie in London and did not expect to win, as she told Variety in a 2023 interview. Raquel Welch accepted the award on her behalf. "It's something that I look back on now and think, 'It would have been so great to be able to have done that,' " Hawn said at the time. During a Feb. 18 appearance on the Today show, Hudson said that she hoped to bring her mom as her Oscars date. "I’m excited just to be doing this again. It’s really cool," she said. "And hopefully my mom will be my date and we can have fun. It’ll be great." Related Stories Hudson also suggested she would bring Hawn to the Oscars during a Feb. 12 interview with Deadline's The Actor's Side series. "I hope she's my date. We'll see. It would be nice," she said at that time. "We'll see how that works too, but I'd like to have my mom on my arm. I'm like, 'I love you [fiancé Danny Fujikawa], but I feel like Mommy might need to be my date for the Oscars.' But we'll see." Robin L Marshall/Getty The actress and singer costarred with Hugh Jackman in Song Sung Blue, a biopic about real-life married musicians Claire “Thunder” Sardina and Mike "Lightning" Sardina, who performed in the Neil Diamond tribute band Lightning & Thunder together for over a decade. The movie is based on a 2008 documentary of the same name. See PEOPLE's coverage of the 98th Academy Awards, airing live on ABC and Hulu on March 15.
